guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why USC is priced as a sizable favorite. We saw the offense produce 461 yards at 7.3 yards per play against Rutgers, and Jayden Maiava has opened the season with 12 touchdown passes against one interception. USC has also converted 65% of its third downs through four games. That efficiency is the clearest concern for our Washington position because it gives USC multiple ways to sustain drives and create separation.

Our disagreement comes from how that offense matches up with Washington’s run defense. Our numbers rate Washington among the nation’s strongest teams in rush EPA, while USC’s rushing efficiency has been much less convincing over the longer run than its latest box score suggests. We also see potential for Washington to find enough on the ground against USC to shorten the game and stay competitive. USC has allowed 43 fourth-quarter points through four games, which does not establish a trend by itself, but it reinforces why we are reluctant to price the Trojans as likely to maintain a wide margin for four quarters.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is USC’s rushing offense against Washington’s front. If Washington can limit efficient early-down runs, USC becomes more dependent on Maiava repeatedly converting through the air rather than controlling the game on schedule. Maiava’s start demands respect, but forcing USC into that narrower path is the most important football reason we see Washington staying inside the available number.

recent_game.fact: USC improved to 4-0 overall and 1-0 in Big Ten play with a 42-35 road victory over Rutgers on Sept. 19.
USC never trailed against Rutgers and produced 461 total yards at 7.3 yards per play, including 5.9 yards per rush and 8.7 yards per pass attempt.
USC scored four offensive touchdowns, one defensive touchdown and two field goals against Rutgers while converting 5 of 10 third downs.
USC forced two Rutgers turnovers, scored 14 points off them and generated 115 interception-return yards.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Jayden Maiava completed 20 of 32 passes for 277 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions against Rutgers.
Through four games, Maiava had completed 87 of 115 passes for 1,173 yards, 12 touchdowns and one interception, with a 75.7% completion rate and 194.0 efficiency rating.
Maiava completed passes to nine different USC players against Rutgers and went 5 of 6 for 35 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter.
Maiava started all 13 games for USC in 2025, completing 265 of 403 passes for 3,711 yards, 24 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while adding six rushing touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running back King Miller rushed 16 times for 102 yards and a touchdown against Rutgers, his second consecutive 100-yard game.
Miller led USC through four games with 338 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 64 carries, averaging 5.3 yards per attempt.
Redshirt freshman running back Riley Wormley produced 54 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on four touches against Rutgers.
Wide receiver Kayden Dixon-Wyatt led USC against Rutgers with five receptions for 77 yards; through four games he led the team with 18 catches for 258 yards and two touchdowns.
Wide receiver Corey Simms caught all four of his targets against Rutgers for a career-high 72 yards, including a 52-yard touchdown on third-and-14.
Freshman tight end Mark Bowman caught three passes for 32 yards against Rutgers after recording six catches for 83 yards and two touchdowns against Louisiana.

USC's offensive line allowed one sack against Rutgers while helping the offense average 5.9 yards per carry; Trojan running backs gained 180 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries without a negative rush.
Offensive lineman Tobias Raymond had started at every offensive-line position except right guard.

defensive_personnel.fact: Safety Prophet Brown intercepted a pass at USC's 1-yard line and returned it 99 yards for a touchdown against Rutgers.
Safety Christian Pierce recorded a game-high 11 tackles, an interception and two pass breakups against Rutgers; USC scored a touchdown two plays after his interception.
Linebacker Deven Bryant led USC with 20 tackles through four games after recording eight against Rutgers.
Bryant previously attended Washington before joining USC.
Defensive end Kameryn Crawford made six tackles and shared USC's only sack against Rutgers with linebacker Desman Stephens II.

injury_availability.fact: Safety Prophet Brown missed the entire 2025 season because of a season-ending injury suffered during fall camp and had returned to play in 2026.
Kicker Caden Chittenden missed the entire 2025 season with a season-ending fall-camp injury and handled USC's place-kicking duties against Rutgers.
Wide receiver Tanook Hines returned from injury against Fresno State and caught an eight-yard touchdown on his first reception of the 2026 season.

offensive_context.fact: Through four games, USC averaged 43.0 points, 500.3 total yards, 324.8 passing yards and 175.5 rushing yards per game.
USC converted 30 of 46 third downs through four games, a 65% conversion rate.
USC scored on 19 of 24 red-zone possessions through four games, including 17 touchdowns.
USC led at halftime in each of its first four games and outscored opponents 106-24 in the first half.

defensive_context.fact: Through four games, USC allowed 317.5 total yards per game, including 113.8 rushing yards and 203.8 passing yards.
USC's defense recorded eight sacks and held opponents to 16 conversions on 42 third-down attempts through four games.
USC allowed only 24 first-half points through four games but allowed 43 points in the fourth quarter.

special_teams.fact: Caden Chittenden made both field-goal attempts and all four PATs against Rutgers in his first game handling USC's place-kicking duties.
Chittenden was perfect through four games, converting both field-goal attempts and all 22 PATs.
Punter Lachlan Carrigan's only punt against Rutgers traveled 56 yards and was downed at the Rutgers 5-yard line; USC had punted exactly once in each of its first four games.
Freshman returner Trent Mosley had an 86-yard punt-return touchdown against Louisiana.
